allOf.description: Inherits shared step-base properties ($schema, id, owner, created_at, canonical_refs_used).

extensions.description: Ordered list of domain-specific extension specs to generate as part of this step. Each entry defines one extension artifact (its ID, schema requirements, and governance anchors). Should contain at least one entry — an empty extensions list indicates no extension work was planned and should be treated as a planning gap.

extension_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this extension, scoped to the project. Format: ext-{NN}-{topic} where NN is a zero-padded sequence number and topic is a short descriptor. Examples: 'ext-01-database', 'ext-02-auth-provider', 'ext-03-payment-gateway'. Should be stable once assigned — renaming breaks downstream traceability. Avoid generic names like 'ext-01-misc'.

title.description: Short, human-readable name for this extension displayed in reports and the trace matrix. Should be title-cased and describe the domain concern clearly (e.g. 'Database Layer Extension', 'Authentication Provider Extension'). Avoid abbreviations.

file_name.description: Output filename for the generated extension artifact. Must follow the pattern 'ext_{NN}_{topic}.json' using underscores as separators and lowercase alphanumerics only. Alignment rule: file_name must be the extension_id with hyphens replaced by underscores and '.json' appended — always derive from extension_id, never invent independently. Side-by-side examples: extension_id='ext-01-data-quality' → file_name='ext_01_data_quality.json'; extension_id='ext-02-ai-features' → file_name='ext_02_ai_features.json'. The file is written to the spec directory alongside the core step artifacts. Anti-pattern: file_name='data_quality_extension.json' (missing the ext_{NN}_ numeric prefix, breaks sort order and traceability); file_name='ext-01-data-quality.json' (uses hyphens — underscores are required so the stem is a valid Python module name for import-based tooling).

area_of_concern.description: High-level domain category this extension addresses. Use a concise noun phrase that classifies the extension's technical scope. Decision rule: when two area names could apply, choose the one that describes the domain concern (the business problem being extended), not the technology implementing it. Canonical disambiguation: 'AI' for user-facing AI features such as recommendation engines, content generation, and AI assistants; 'ML' for model training pipelines, experimentation frameworks, and model management infrastructure; 'Payments' for payment processing flows, transaction management, and financial reconciliation; 'Data' for ETL pipelines, analytics schemas, and data quality frameworks. Examples: an LLM-powered chat feature → 'AI'; a model retraining pipeline → 'ML'; a Stripe integration → 'Payments'; a dbt pipeline → 'Data'. Other accepted values: 'Security', 'Notifications', 'Infrastructure'. Anti-pattern: 'General', 'Other', 'Misc' — these defeat the purpose of domain-specific extensions and will be flagged by canonical-lint; every extension must have a specific, nameable concern.

justification.description: Rationale explaining why this extension is necessary and why it could not be covered by the core spec steps. Should reference the specific gap, risk, or domain need. A weak justification ('it is needed') is insufficient — cite the driving functional requirement, NFR, or governance rule. Minimum one substantive sentence.

required_schema_sections.description: Schema sections that should be present in any valid extension generated by this template. Each entry identifies a mandatory structural element. Use to enforce non-negotiable quality gates — for example, every extension should have a 'trace' section and a 'validation_rules' section. Extensions that omit required sections fail the extension generator validation. Should contain at least the sections that establish traceability and governance for the extension.

items.description: Exact key name of a section that must appear in the generated extension schema. Use the exact JSON key as it will appear in the schema's properties. Common sections by area_of_concern: for 'Data' → 'entities', 'schemas', 'migrations'; for 'Security' → 'policies', 'threat_models', 'access_controls'; for 'Payments' → 'providers', 'transaction_types', 'reconciliation'; for 'AI/ML' → 'models', 'evaluation_criteria', 'data_lineage'. Always include 'trace' and 'validation_rules' as minimum sections regardless of area_of_concern. Anti-pattern: 'general', 'other', 'misc' — every section name should be domain-specific.

schema_design_guidelines.description: Prose guidance for the AI or author generating this extension's JSON schema. Must specify: (1) which canonical $defs from schema/core/ must be reused rather than redefined, (2) any ID format patterns for objects within the extension, (3) structural constraints unique to this domain, and (4) what to avoid. Decision rule: guidelines are sufficient when any reviewer could implement the schema without making structural choices — if a guideline leaves the implementer guessing, it is too vague. Example for 'Payments': '(1) reuse vc:core:atoms#httpMethod for method fields rather than redefining; (2) all payment entry IDs follow pay-{noun}-{n} pattern; (3) every payment entry must include currency_code (ISO 4217 three-letter code) and amount_cents (non-negative integer); (4) avoid hardcoding currency symbols in enum values — use codes only.' Example for 'Security': '(1) reuse vc:core:atoms#severityLevel for risk fields; (2) all control IDs follow ctrl-{category}-{n}; (3) every control must include enforcement_layer from the approved enum.' Anti-pattern: generic guidelines like 'follow good naming conventions' that do not specify which atoms to reuse or what structural constraints apply — these provide no actionable constraint and will be silently ignored by generators.

tag_ref.description: Canonical reference to a tag in the canonical registry that categorises this extension. Kind must be 'term'. Example: {"id": "cn:project:term:payments", "kind": "term", "label": "payments"}. Used by canonical-lint to validate that extension tags resolve to known categories. Define the tag in canon/manifest.json before referencing it here.

policy_ref.description: Canonical reference to the governance policy that applies to this extension. Kind must be 'risk_category'. Example: {"id": "cn:project:risk_category:pci-dss", "kind": "risk_category", "label": "PCI-DSS"}. Reference when the extension area has a specific compliance framework or organisational policy governing it. Strict mode: when policy_ref is present, the extension schema must include a 'policies' section.

id_pattern_ref.description: Canonical reference to the ID naming pattern used for items in this extension. Kind must be 'term' or 'action'. Include only when the extension schema uses a non-standard ID pattern (e.g., dot-separated namespaces, UUID-based IDs). Omit when IDs follow the standard kebab-case pattern enforced by `vc:core:atoms#kebabId` — the default pattern applies automatically. Example for non-standard: {"id": "cn:project:term:uuid-pattern", "kind": "term", "label": "uuid-pattern"} for an extension requiring UUID-formatted IDs. Validated by canonical-integrity lint to ensure extension IDs conform to the registered pattern. Anti-pattern: adding id_pattern_ref to reference the standard kebab-case pattern (it's the default — omitting the field achieves the same result).

governance_label_ref.description: Canonical reference to the governance label applied to this extension. Kind must be 'capability'. Reference the canonical governance label for this extension's review tier. Example: {"id": "cn:core:term:security-review-required", "kind": "term", "label": "security-review-required"}. Required field — validated by canonical-integrity lint. This label links the extension to the governance framework that controls its lifecycle (creation, modification, deprecation). If the governance label is not yet in the canon, add a canonical_proposals entry for it instead of fabricating an ID. Define the label in canon/manifest.json before referencing it here. Anti-pattern: referencing a governance_label_ref ID that does not exist in canon/manifest.json — canonical-integrity lint will fail at build time.

items.description: A single extension spec definition. Bundles the extension's identity (extension_id, title, file_name), domain scope (area_of_concern), rationale (justification), structural requirements (required_schema_sections, schema_design_guidelines), and canonical registry anchors (tag_ref, policy_ref, id_pattern_ref, governance_label_ref).
